target_customer: Boutique and mid-size recruitment agencies, executive search firms and independent recruiters
problem: Agency recruiters juggle generic ATS tools and CRMs such as HubSpot that do not fit outbound sourcing; Crew merges ATS and CRM with LinkedIn integration.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription per seat (pricing not found)
product_category: ATS and CRM for recruiting agencies

founders.name: Amine Skalli
prior_employers: A bicycle company (built an e-commerce unit, per TechCrunch)
previous_startups: Recruiting marketplace for remote software engineers (unnamed, per YC page)
founders.background_notes: YC page: professional recruiter for 4 years and co-founded a recruiting marketplace; TechCrunch says he recruited teams for 10 years. Education not found.

founders.name: Ruben Guenoun
founders.background_notes: Named as co-founder and CRO by Tech.eu (Feb 2023); TechCrunch spells the name Gueunoun; the YC page lists only Skalli. No background found.

competitors.name: Lever
competitors.what: General ATS and recruiting CRM for in-house teams

technical_complexity.rationale: A CRM and ATS with LinkedIn integration and some AI features; standard SaaS where LinkedIn data access is the fragile part.

defensibility.rationale: Agencies keep candidate and client data in it, but Bullhorn, Loxo, Recruit CRM and others offered the same combination.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No source shows incumbents copying Crew specifically; the market stayed crowded and Crew remained independent.

market_need_then: The founder says agency recruiters struggled with ATS tools and fell back on HubSpot, motivating a 'HubSpot for recruiting'; Crew reported 100 paying customers after about 18 months in beta.

branding.domain_note: Uses crew.work, a .work TLD, rather than crew.com.

identity.visual_style: Company description calls the product beautiful and well designed
identity.voice_and_tone: Casual and playful, with phrases like 'cool automation and even a dash of AI' on the YC page.

brand_strength.rationale: Short friendly word but extremely generic and shared with other companies named Crew; TechCrunch coverage covered the product not the brand.

outcome_analysis: Crew spent roughly 18 months in closed beta after YC Summer 2021, then launched publicly in February 2023 with a $2.3M seed and about 100 paying customers. It remains small with six to eight people reported and no later round, exit or shutdown found. The niche is crowded with established ATS and agency CRM vendors, so the outcome is still open.
notes: TechCrunch says 2.45M raised to date while Tech.eu says a 2.3M seed; Welcome to the Jungle (via search snippet) lists 2.5M across two seed rounds including one in Sept 2021, and CB Insights 2.43M over 3 rounds. The Sept 2021 round is only in aggregator snippets, so not recorded. Crew.work site fetch returned 503, so site content could not be verified. Competitors Lever, Greenhouse and Workable are named in a Feb 2023 source, about 20 months after the batch; all existed well before 2021 but no pre-batch dated source was found. Crew launched out of the eFounders studio per TechCrunch.
